tool.name: PlotDesigner

summary.para:
View online help files: https://www.jennessent.com/geometric-tools/plot-designer.html
Lays out a block of rectangular research plots -- so many plots end to end along a plot direction and so many side by side across it, each of a given length and width -- and repeats the block for every replication, assigning the rate values to the plots in a fresh random order each time. The block starts at an anchor point (the back-left corner of the first plot, facing along the direction) that you type here or click on the map in the Plot Designer window, where the direction can also be drawn on the map to match a fenceline. Distances are geodesic-true. Writes the plot polygons and, optionally, their center points and long-axis centerlines, each carrying Rep, Plot, Plot_ID and Rate. A port of the CropCentric Plot Designer (Jenness and Wiebers 2018). Works at every license level.

tool.usage:
The block. Plots are rectangles of the given length (along the plot direction) and width (across it). Plots along the direction are placed end to end and plots across side by side, so each replication holds length-count x width-count plots, and the rate list must hold exactly one value per plot. Every replication receives the same rate values in a fresh random order (the classic randomized block); give a random seed to repeat an order.
Where it goes. The anchor is the back-left corner of the first plot when you stand on it facing along the plot direction: plots extend forward along the bearing and to the right across it. Type the anchor's X and Y (in the coordinate system you name, else the field layer's, else the output's), or leave them empty and give a field layer, whose extent's lower-left corner (the selection's extent when features are selected) is used. The Plot Designer window lets you click the anchor and draw the direction on the map with a live preview.
Replications are laid side by side (across the direction) or end to end (along it), separated by the gap.
Geometry. Everything is built in an azimuthal equidistant projection centered on the anchor, on the output coordinate system's own datum, so every edge has its true ground length and the bearing is a true bearing -- then projected to the output coordinate system (the field layer's, the anchor's, or the Output Coordinate System environment).
Outputs. The plot polygons carry Unique_ID, Rep, Plot (counted along the direction first, then across), Plot_ID (R<rep>P<plot>), Rate, Center_X and Center_Y (output coordinate system), Center_Lon and Center_Lat, Bearing, Long_m and Short_m. The optional center points and centerlines carry the same fields; the centerline runs along each plot's long axis. Shapefile outputs work. Feed the polygons to Fuse Plots and Field to make the prescription map, and to Add Random Numbers for any further random assignment.

dialogReference.para: The plot polygons, one per plot of every replication, with Rep, Plot, Plot_ID, Rate, center coordinates, bearing and edge lengths. A geodatabase feature class or a shapefile.
The long edge of each plot, in the units below.
The short edge of each plot, in the units below.

param.name: units
param.displayname: Units of the plot length, width and gap

dialogReference.para: Meters, Feet, US survey feet, Yards, Kilometers or Miles. Distances are measured along the ground, whatever the map's projection.

param.name: bearing
param.displayname: Plot direction (bearing in degrees clockwise from north)

dialogReference.para: The direction of the plots' long edges: 0 = north, 90 = east. In the Plot Designer window it can be drawn on the map.

param.name: n_long
param.displayname: Plots along the direction (end to end)

dialogReference.para: How many plots end to end along the plot direction in each replication.

param.name: n_short
param.displayname: Plots across the direction (side by side)

dialogReference.para: How many plots side by side across the plot direction in each replication.

param.name: rates
param.displayname: Rate values, one per plot, separated by commas

dialogReference.para: The treatment values, exactly one per plot of a replication (plots along x plots across), separated by commas. Each replication gets them in a fresh random order.
How many times the block is repeated.

param.name: field_layer
param.displayname: Field polygon layer (optional; supplies the coordinate system and a default anchor)

dialogReference.para: The field or fields the plots go in. Gives the output its coordinate system and, when no anchor is typed, the anchor: the lower-left corner of the layer's extent (its selection's extent when features are selected).
X of the anchor point, the back-left corner of the first plot. Give both X and Y, or neither.

param.name: anchor_cs
param.displayname: Coordinate system of the anchor (default: the field layer's, else the output's)

dialogReference.para: The coordinate system the anchor X and Y are given in. The Plot Designer window passes the map's.
Side by side (across the plot direction): each replication sits to the right of the one before. End to end (along the plot direction): each replication continues forward along the direction.

param.name: rep_gap
param.displayname: Gap between replications (in the units above)

dialogReference.para: Optional point feature class of the plot centers, with the same fields as the polygons.

param.name: out_lines
param.displayname: Output plot centerlines (along the long edge)

dialogReference.para: Optional line feature class: each plot's centerline along its long axis, with the same fields as the polygons.

param.name: seed
param.displayname: Random seed (optional; repeats the same rate order)

dialogReference.para: Any whole number. The same seed with the same inputs repeats the same random order of rates.

scriptExample.title: Plot Designer example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Four replications of a 2 x 3 block of 40 x 20 m plots at a bearing of 30 degrees, anchored at a typed UTM corner, with center points.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.jenness.PlotDesigner( out_fc=r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Plots_2026", long_edge=40, short_edge=20, units="Meters", bearing=30, n_long=2, n_short=3, rates="0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250", n_reps=4, field_layer=r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Fields", anchor_x=441250.0, anchor_y=3895120.0, anchor_cs=arcpy.SpatialReference(26912), rep_layout="Side by side (across the plot direction)", rep_gap=5, out_points=r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Plots_2026_Points", seed=7)
